generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL; never overwritten by any planter (ties, nulls, group_sizes, different_values) — planters must exclude PK columns.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from parent PK pool (existing parent rows only); allow NULL with probability 0.15 when nullable; NEVER emit orphan values (no parent PK + 1000); unmatched_join_rows is satisfied only by NULL child FKs and by parent rows with no children.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in [min-1, max+1] of observed range; include boundary values at each listed literal and one step on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform real rounded to 1 decimal in [min-1, max+1]; include boundary values at each listed literal and one step on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from observed value pool; enforce 20-50% duplicate share on non-PK, non-FK text columns by capping fresh distinct values; add near-variants (case changes, trailing space, empty string) with probability 0.10.
generic_sampling_rules.text_date: Sample from observed date-string pool; preserve format; add one-day-shifted variants for boundary testing.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Sample from observed distinct values; ensure each value appears at least once; boundary values listed in per_column_exceptions are injected into the enum pool (not ignored); add near-variants (case changes, empty string) with probability 0.10.
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: For every nullable column, each instance contains at least one NULL row; NULL share follows compact database share (5-30% for columns with null_rows pattern, 0% otherwise); planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule; planters run in order nulls -> group_sizes -> ties -> different_values, and each planter excludes PK columns and re-verifies prior structures.
generic_sampling_rules.planter_order: nulls, then group_sizes, then ties, then different_values; each planter excludes PK columns; after all planters, re-verify group-size and tie structures and re-plant if overwritten.

targets.rule: Parent rows without children: at least one artist with no volume, one volume with no music_festival. Child rows with NULL FK: volume.Artist_ID and music_festival.Volume get NULL in 5-30% of rows. No orphan (non-NULL, non-existent) FK values are permitted; foreign_keys pragma must be ON during insert.

Duplicate share 20-50% on these non-PK, non-FK DISTINCT columns; ensure COUNT(DISTINCT col) < COUNT(col). PK columns (artist.Artist_ID, music_festival.ID) and FK column volume.Artist_ID are excluded (PKs cannot duplicate; FK duplicates arise naturally from FK sampling).

NULL share 5-30% of generated rows; at least one NULL row per column per instance; _plant_nulls must actually set NULLs in music_festival.Result (verify Result is in cols and not overwritten by later planters).

At least two rows tie at rank 1 for DESC order on artist.Age and artist.Artist; artist.Artist_ID is a PK and is excluded from tie planting (PKs must stay unique). For music_festival.Result ensure ties at rank 1 and rank 100 on COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT id) in both ASC and DESC.

artist.Age: include values 22,23,24,25,26,31,32,33. music_festival.Result: include 'Nominated','nominated','','x','NOMINATED' — these are injected into the EnumSampler pool; the enum formula for Result is relaxed to allow these boundary variants (see semantic_rules_and_formulas). volume.Weeks_on_Top: include 1,2,3.
Ensure at least 2 rows per group with different values for MAX/SUM/AVG and MIN aggregates.

Group sizes for music_festival.Result must include groups of size 1, 2, and >=3; when fewer than 3 distinct values exist, draw from the enum/observed pool or synthesize distinct values rather than collapsing to pool[0].
Ensure at least one Category group has COUNT(*) > 2 and at least one has COUNT(*) <= 1; requires a dedicated aggregate_boundary planter.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: integrity.fk_violations = 56 and validity.invalid = 19/20 with reason 'new_integrity_failures'. The writer (writer.py) sets 'pragma foreign_keys = OFF' before inserting generated rows, so FK violations are never caught at insert time; the orphan-FK rule (parent PK + 1000) in instance.py fill_foreign_keys_consistently injects orphan values into volume.Artist_ID and music_festival.Volume, and _plant_parent_without_child can also leave dangling references. The spec's unmatched_join_rows rule only asks for parent rows without children and child rows with NULL FK — it does not authorize orphan (non-NULL, non-existent) FK values.
issues.requested_revision: Do not emit orphan FK values (parent PK + 1000) for volume.Artist_ID or music_festival.Volume; the unmatched_join_rows target is satisfied by NULL child FKs and by parent rows with no children. Either remove the orphan injection or restrict it to columns where the specification explicitly permits orphan values. Additionally, enable 'pragma foreign_keys = ON' (or validate FKs before commit) so that any residual FK violation is caught and counted rather than silently written.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: rows_skipped.artist = 86 out of 128 attempted (42 added). The artist table has a single-column PK (Artist_ID) and the writer inserts generated rows with executemany; the fallback row-by-row path skips rows that violate constraints. instance.py _next_pk starts after the compact max, but _plant_ties / _plant_different_values / _plant_nulls run after PK assignment and can overwrite Artist_ID values (ties rule targets artist.Artist_ID), producing duplicate PKs that are then skipped. This silently discards ~67% of generated artist rows and undermines the ties_for_order_limit rule for artist.Artist_ID.
issues.requested_revision: Exclude primary-key columns from _plant_ties, _plant_nulls, _plant_different_values and _plant_group_sizes (or re-assign PKs after planting). Ensure generated PKs remain unique and sequential so that no generated row is skipped for PK reasons; report rows_skipped.artist near zero.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic_rules_and_formulas: music_festival.Result formula 'Result IN (\'Nominated\',\'Awarded\') OR Result IS NULL' and Category formula 'Category IN (\'Best Song\',\'Best Lyrics\',\'Best Sound Song\') OR Category IS NULL'. But per_column_exceptions comparison_boundary for music_festival.Result requires values 'Nominated','nominated','','x','NOMINATED', and text_short/text_enum generic rules add near-variants (case changes, empty string) with probability 0.10. These two requirements conflict: the enum formula forbids 'nominated', '', 'x', 'NOMINATED', while the boundary rule requires them. The program resolves this by passing boundaries only to NumberSampler (values.py make_column_sampler ignores boundaries for EnumSampler), so the Result boundary values are never generated — the comparison_boundary target for music_festival.Result is unimplemented.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the specification: either drop the enum formula for music_festival.Result (allowing the boundary variants) or drop the boundary variants from the comparison_boundary target. If boundary variants are intended, the program must inject them into the EnumSampler pool; if not, remove them from the spec so the program and spec agree.

issues.evidence: values.py make_column_sampler: 'boundaries' is only forwarded to NumberSampler; EnumSampler and StringSampler ignore it. spec.py stores boundaries for music_festival.Result ('Nominated','nominated','','x','NOMINATED') but they are never used. Similarly, spec_for returns 'aggregate_boundary' for music_festival.Category but instance.py has no planter for aggregate_boundary (only _plant_group_sizes, _plant_ties, _plant_different_values, _plant_nulls), so the aggregate_boundary rule (COUNT(*) > 2 and <= 1 per Category group) is not implemented by construction.
issues.requested_revision: Implement boundary injection for text/enum columns (add boundary values to the EnumSampler/StringSampler element pool) and add an aggregate_boundary planter that guarantees at least one Category group with COUNT(*) > 2 and one with COUNT(*) <= 1. issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_group_sizes: 'v1, v2, v3 = rng.sample(pool, 3) if len(set(map(str, pool))) >= 3 else (pool[0], pool[0], pool[0])'. When fewer than 3 distinct values exist, all three are set to pool[0], so group sizes 1, 2, >=3 are not actually created. Also _plant_ties and _plant_different_values can overwrite the group-size assignments afterwards (planters run in order: nulls, group_sizes, ties, different_values), potentially destroying the 1/2/>=3 structure. The ties_for_order_limit target for music_festival.Result ('ties at rank 1 and rank 100 on COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT id) in both ASC and DESC') is not implemented at all — _plant_ties only creates two equal values, not rank-100 ties.
issues.requested_revision: Make _plant_group_sizes robust when fewer than 3 distinct values exist (draw from the enum/observed pool or synthesize distinct values). Reorder planters so that group-size and tie structures are not overwritten, or re-verify after planting. Implement the rank-100 tie requirement for music_festival.Result or remove it from the specification.

issues.evidence: instance.py fill_foreign_keys_consistently: 'nullable = not cm.notnull and cm.pk_pos == 0'. For volume.Artist_ID and music_festival.Volume the schema declares them as plain INT (not NOT NULL), so nullable is True and NULLs are planted — consistent with the spec. However, the same function also applies orphan values (base + 1000) to non-NULL FK values with probability orphan_prob=0.10, which is the source of the 56 FK violations. The spec's unmatched_join_rows rule does not request orphan values, only NULL child FKs and parent rows without children.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the orphan-value branch from fill_foreign_keys_consistently (or gate it behind an explicit spec flag that is not set for this database). Keep NULL child FKs and parent-without-child planting, which satisfy the unmatched_join_rows target without violating referential integrity.

issues.evidence: Specification supporting_evidence: 'Artist name duplicates observed (5 distinct of 7 rows) but no formula.' The duplicates_for_distinct rule targets artist.Artist_ID, music_festival.ID, volume.Artist_ID, volume.Song, volume.Issue_Date, artist.Famous_Title, music_festival.Category with 'Duplicate share 20-50%'. issues.evidence: `_plant_parent_without_child` only sets `vals[0] = unused[0]` for the first child row, which may be overwritten by `_plant_nulls` (which runs before it in the loop, but `_plant_parent_without_child` runs after the per-table loop, so it is not overwritten). However, `_plant_parent_without_child` is called once after all tables are built, and it only handles the first unused parent per FK; if `vals[0]` is NULL (planted by `_plant_nulls`), it is replaced with a non-NULL unused parent, which is fine. The construction is sound but fragile: it assumes `vals[0]` is not the only child row pointing at the unused parent.
